summary: Summarizes the X.500 information model for collective attributes, which let entries in a collection share common characteristics, and describes their use in LDAP. It provides schema definitions for collective attributes. It is a proposed standard.

eli5.summary: Instead of writing the same office address on every employee card, you write it once for the whole group. This lets a directory share one fact across many entries.

questions: what is an ldap collective attribute
how do collective attributes work in ldap
what does the c- prefix mean in ldap attributes
subtitle: How a directory can store a value once and show it on every entry in a group.

tldr.problem: Many directory entries share the same details, such as an office address or phone number, and keeping a copy in every entry is wasteful and easy to get wrong.
tldr.mechanism: Collective attributes are stored once in a collective attribute subentry and appear as read-only values on every entry within that subentry's scope. The RFC defines the operational attributes that manage them and 13 ready-made collective attribute types.
tldr.outcome: A directory can share common values across a collection of entries while individual entries can still opt out through collectiveExclusions.

facts.label: Naming convention
facts.value: c- prefix on the supertype name

today: RFC 3671 is a Proposed Standard from December 2003, and the unit metadata lists no RFC that obsoletes or updates it.

sections.title: Sharing Values Across Entries
sections.content:
In X.500, a collective attribute is a user attribute whose values are the same for each member of an entry collection. RFC 3671 describes how to use them in the Lightweight Directory Access Protocol (LDAP). It summarizes the X.500 information model and provides the schema definitions LDAP needs.

An entry collection is a group of object and alias entries that share some property or relationship. A collection consists of all the entries within the scope of a collective attributes subentry, and one entry can belong to several collections.
sections.eli5: Think of a class of students who all share the same school address. You write the address once on the class sign instead of on every student.

sections.title: How Collective Attributes Behave
sections.content:
Clients can see the values of a collective attribute on each entry in the collection, but cannot update them there. The values are changed through the associated collective attributes subentry instead.

When an entry belongs to several collections, its values for each collective attribute are combined, so clients do not see the independent sources of those values. An entry can leave a particular collective attribute out by listing it in its collectiveExclusions attribute. Like other user attributes, collective attributes are subject to access, administrative and content controls.
sections.eli5: You can read the shared sign on any card, but only the person in charge of the class sign can change it. A student can also ask not to have a certain line shown on their card.

sections.title: The System Schema
sections.content:
Three schema elements manage collective attributes. LDAP servers MUST act in accordance with the X.500 Directory Models when providing this service.

  • collectiveAttributeSubentry (OID 2.5.17.2) is an auxiliary object class. Subentries of this class administer collective attributes. A subentry SHOULD contain at least one collective attribute, and those attributes can be found, searched and compared at every entry in its scope.
  • collectiveAttributeSubentries (OID 2.5.18.12) is an operational attribute that identifies all collective attribute subentries affecting an entry. It is marked NO-USER-MODIFICATION.
  • collectiveExclusions (OID 2.5.18.7) is an operational attribute that MAY appear in any entry and MAY have multiple values. Each value excludes one collective attribute from that entry.

If the descriptor excludeAllCollectiveAttributes (OID 2.5.18.0) or its OID is a value of collectiveExclusions, all collective attributes are excluded from the entry.

Implementations SHOULD support collective attribute subentries in both collectiveAttributeSpecificArea (2.5.23.5) and collectiveAttributeInnerArea (2.5.23.6) administrative areas.
sections.eli5: There is a special class sign, a note on each card saying which class signs apply, and an opt-out list. One magic word on the opt-out list means skip every class sign.

sections.title: Defining Collective Attribute Types
sections.content:
An attribute type from the userApplications usage can be defined to be COLLECTIVE. That means the same values appear in the entries of a collection, subject to collectiveExclusions and other administrative controls such as DIT content rules, if implemented.

Collective attributes are commonly defined as subtypes of ordinary attributes. By convention the name is the supertype's name with a c- prefix, so the collective version of telephoneNumber is c-TelephoneNumber.

The RFC sets firm limits:

  • Non-collective attribute types SHALL NOT subtype collective attributes.
  • Collective attributes SHALL NOT be SINGLE-VALUED.
  • Collective attribute types SHALL NOT appear in the attribute types of an object class definition.
  • Operational attributes SHALL NOT be defined to be collective.
sections.eli5: A shared line on the class sign gets the same name as the personal line with a c- in front, like c-TelephoneNumber. A shared line must be allowed to hold more than one value.

sections.title: The Predefined Collective Attributes
sections.content:

sections.eli5: The RFC supplies ready-made shared lines for common things like city, street, office name and phone number, so every directory uses the same names.

sections.title: Security and IANA Registration
sections.content:
Collective attributes are subject to access control restrictions and other administrative policy. Generally, collective attributes read through an entry in a collection follow the rules for attributes of that entry, and those accessed through a subentry follow the rules for attributes of the subentry. Because LDAP has no standard access model, the details depend on each server's access control system. General LDAP security considerations also apply.

The IANA registered the LDAP descriptors defined here. The RFC makes no OID assignments: it reuses existing X.500 schema elements assigned by ISO/IEC JTC 1 SC 6.
sections.eli5: Who may see or change the shared lines depends on each directory's own rules, because LDAP does not set one standard rulebook for that.

items.title: collectiveAttributeSubentry
items.text: Auxiliary object class (2.5.17.2) for the subentry that holds the shared values.

items.title: collectiveAttributeSubentries
items.text: Operational attribute (2.5.18.12) listing the subentries that affect an entry.

items.title: collectiveExclusions
items.text: Operational attribute (2.5.18.7) that excludes chosen collective attributes from an entry.
